authorReview.reason: Candidate: four quokkas crowded in shade beneath a bench, hard sunlight at the edge. Large foreground animal has lowered head and mostly closed eyes. No literal sequence proved.

candidate.title: The patch she left
candidate.subject: quokka
candidate.body:
I watched her leave the shadow. Slid into the patch she'd left and shut my eyes before she came back.

Something touched my shoulder. I let my head droop. Something else stepped on my tail.

I was prepared to sleep very convincingly.

Then a warm flank pressed against me. Another body settled against that one. By the time I opened my eyes, we were all under the bench and I couldn't remember which bit I had stolen.

The sun reached one foot. I moved it inward. Three quokkas adjusted themselves.

My foot was in the shade. My other one wasn't.
candidate.visibleScene: Four quokkas clustered beneath a bench on hard ground. Foreground right adult-sized animal has a lowered head and mostly closed eyes. Their bodies are close, with a strong boundary between shade and bright sun nearby.

preservedHeldProse.title: An opening appeared
preservedHeldProse.literalBody: The big quokka left the cool spot. I moved in before the flattened grass could stand up. She returned almost immediately. I shut my eyes with enormous conviction.

preservedHeldProse.title: One foot outside
preservedHeldProse.literalBody: The shade was just wide enough until the sun moved. Pulled my foot in. The other foot went out. I am beginning to understand why the larger quokka arrived before me.
preservedHeldProse.status: held unillustrated passage remains unchanged; not spent admission

preservedHeldProse.title: White fur, dark stones
preservedHeldProse.literalBody:
My coat had begun coming loose in pale tufts. Rubbed against a rock and left a little of winter on its edge.

Underneath I was darker. The bare ground no longer made me look like something that had wandered into the wrong season.

Sat in a sunny patch and pulled at another loose tuft. It stuck to my lip. A great deal of looking appropriate involves looking ridiculous first.
